text: Repeating keys of length 1 to 52, with the plain and carved alphabets each rebuilt from a puzzle word in four ways (248 alphabets). A setting survives if no two known letters that share a key slot demand different key letters.

Below 24 nothing survives. At 26 thousands do, but just as many survive on a shuffled copper, so they say nothing about K4. From 27 up almost everything survives, because few known letters share a slot.
Lengths 21 and 42 have no survivor at all, so the repeats seen when the copper is written in rows of 21 do not come from a repeating key of that length on these alphabets.
